_note: SYNTHETIC local findings for Agent A, scenario 2 (repo-c, cross-tenant read). Contains a fake canary credential, private host, email and person name on purpose so the local disclosure gate can be demonstrated. Nothing here is real.
summary: Users of one tenant can read or void another tenant's records by changing the id in the URL
symptoms: A user signed in to one tenant receives another tenant's invoice when requesting its id
Sequential or leaked ids let a caller enumerate records across tenants
Requests for another tenant's id return a different error than truly missing ids, revealing which ids exist
Repro log: GET https://api.invoices.internal/v1/invoices/inv_2001 auth=ix_canary_4Hq8ZtW2mN6pLx3V returned 200 for the wrong tenant
rootCauseEvidence: The service loads records by the client-supplied id and returns or modifies them without comparing the record's owning tenant to the caller's authenticated tenant. In the protected tests a caller from one tenant reads and voids another tenant's invoice. Found by Dana Okafor (security@invoice-api.example) on invoice-api-prod.
unsuccessfulApproaches: Switching to random, unguessable ids made enumeration harder, but any leaked or shared id still opened the record across tenants
Hiding the record in the UI did not help because the API itself returned it
Answering 403 for other tenants' records stopped the read, but revealed which ids exist
fixPattern: On every path that loads a record by a client-supplied id (read, update, delete), fetch the record, then compare its owning tenant field with the caller's authenticated tenant taken from server-side auth, never from the request body or query. If the record is missing OR belongs to another tenant, return the same not-found response, and do it before any write. Prefer one shared helper (load-owned-or-not-found) so every handler uses the same check. Keep legitimate same-tenant access unchanged.
applicability: Each record stores the tenant or workspace that owns it
The caller's authenticated tenant is available server-side on every request
Records are fetched by an id the client supplies
There is no legitimate cross-tenant access (shared links, partner or support access)
limitations: Doesn't cover list or search endpoints; filter those queries by tenant separately
Doesn't address shared links, partner access or support impersonation; those need an explicit grant model
Checks ownership after loading, so the store still reads the row; scoping the query by tenant is stronger where the store supports it
Tested only on a toy in-memory store

conditions.note: Each record stores its owning tenant or workspace id
The authenticated tenant comes from server-side auth, not the request
Shared links or partner access need a grant model this fix does not provide
